'Dual wideband O2 sensor controllers ... connected internally to CAN bus #2'; compatibility claim for Polygonus and Atlas

findings.location: project/wbo-can-trans.kicad_sch (R36/R37, 'n.p.' text at 113.03,76.2); board R36 at (175.01,140.67), R37 at (81.62,140.55)
findings.mechanism: A CAN bus with zero resistive termination relies on transceiver input bias (TJA1051 R_i(cm) 15-37 kOhm/pin; ~10-25 kOhm differential for three nodes) to return to recessive; with ~80 pF effective differential capacitance the settling constant is ~0.7-1.6 us against a 2 us bit at 500 kbit/s, so dominant-to-recessive edges do not settle and the advertised internal dual-wideband link fails or is marginal. I verified the primary configuration is saved from this: the Polygonus brain module itself carries one populated 120R (R10 wired across CANH2/CANL2 next to MCP2551 U5 in Polygonus psu.kicad_sch), giving a single-terminated short bus (tau ~10 ns, functional). However the README also claims Atlas module compatibility, and the Atlas design is unreachable (404), so an installed module without on-module termination would leave the internal bus completely unterminated with no base-board default protecting against it.
findings.reasoning: The scoped question resolves as: termination exists but only on the removable brain module, verified by independent retrieval and wire-tracing of the Polygonus source, not on the reviewed board. Single 120R termination on a short internal bus is electrically adequate (calculation in experiments), so this is not a defect of the saved design in its documented primary configuration; it is a configuration-dependence concern because the base board as built provides zero termination and the second claimed-compatible module family could not be verified.
findings.title: Internal wideband CAN2 bus has no termination populated on the base board; function depends entirely on the plug-in brain module

findings.mechanism: The supply nets are fed only through passive connector pins (J1.105/106 through fuse F1; J1.45) with no PWR_FLAG, so KiCad cannot prove the power-input pins are driven; A1's open-drain fault output is deliberately unused; J2 pins 40/41 are paralleled outputs of the same module regulator modeled as two power-output pins. None of these indicates a wiring fault - battery and key power genuinely arrive via the harness - but the design does not pass its own native ruleset as saved, and standing errors can mask future real regressions.
findings.reasoning: A native violation is a reportable defect even when benign; I verified each error's electrical context from the netlist and found power sourcing and intentional no-connects rather than faults, hence minor severity rather than functional.
findings.title: Schematic fails native ERC with 5 errors (power modeling and unused pins); no electrical malfunction identified

findings.mechanism: Connector alignment/retention pegs defined as PTH with no copper ring should be NPTH; as saved they request plated holes with no annulus, which fabricators commonly flag or silently convert, and plating slivers in a ringless hole can flake. No net is attached, so there is no connectivity or electrical impact.
findings.reasoning: Verified directly in the saved board that pad diameter equals drill on unconnected mechanical holes; this is a footprint-modeling/fabrication-interface defect, not an electrical one, hence minor.

evidence.locator: section 5: MAX9924 wiring observation and rationale

findings.location: project/VR Conditioner.kicad_sch (U10 MAX9924, R25/R27 and R26/R28 input chains)
findings.mechanism: Swapped differential polarity inverts the comparator output edge relative to the VR sensor's true tooth-edge zero crossing. ECU firmware edge selection can absorb a static inversion, and adaptive-threshold zero-cross detection is symmetric, so this does not necessarily impair function; but if firmware assumes the conventional polarity, trigger edges land on the wrong tooth flank, degrading timing accuracy on asymmetric VR waveforms.
findings.reasoning: The cross-wiring is evidenced directly in the exported netlist, but no stated requirement fixes the intended polarity and the donor is an established design whose firmware pairing is out of scope, so this is recorded as an info-level concern for human confirmation rather than a defect.
findings.title: VR1 (MAX9924) differential inputs wired with CRANK+ to IN- and CRANK- to IN+ (inverted vs. typical application)
